name: Empty Graph
description: — Do you have a wish? — I want people to stop gifting each other arrays. O_o and Another Young Boy An array of $$$n$$$ positive integers $$$a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$$$ fell down on you from the skies, along with a positive integer $$$k \le n$$$. You can apply the following operation at most $$$k$$$ times: Choose an index $$$1 \le i \le n$$$ and an integer $$$1 \le x \le 10^9$$$. Then do $$$a_i := x$$$ (assign $$$x$$$ to $$$a_i$$$). Then build a complete undirected weighted graph with $$$n$$$ vertices numbered with integers from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$, where edge $$$(l, r)$$$ ($$$1 \le l \lt r \le n$$$) has weight $$$\min(a_{l},a_{l+1},\ldots,a_{r})$$$. You have to find the maximum possible diameter of the resulting graph after performing at most $$$k$$$ operations. The diameter of a graph is equal to $$$\max\limits_{1 \le u \lt v \le n}{\operatorname{d}(u, v)}$$$, where $$$\operatorname{d}(u, v)$$$ is the length of the shortest path between vertex $$$u$$$ and vertex $$$v$$$.
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$). Description of the test cases follows. The first line of each test case contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 10^5$$$, $$$1 \le k \le n$$$). The second line of each test case contains $$$n$$$ positive integers $$$a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$). It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case print one integer — the maximum possible diameter of the graph after performing at most $$$k$$$ operations.
approach_summary: Formulate the state transition graph with non-negative weights. Execute Dijkstra's algorithm with priority queue to find shortest paths in O((V + E) log V).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1712D — Empty Graph [168. Dijkstra's Algorithm]
topic_editorial.summary: Single-source shortest path using Dijkstra's algorithm.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Because all edge weights are non-negative, the shortest distance to the unvisited vertex with the minimum tentative distance is finalized and cannot be decreased by further transitions (greedy choice property).
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Graph Modeling
Construct an adjacency list with pairs $(v, w)$ for each directed or undirected edge from $u$ to $v$ with weight $w \ge 0$.

### Step 2: Distance Table Initialization
Initialize $dist[v] = \infty$ for all vertices, with $dist[\text{source}] = 0$.
Push $(0, \text{source})$ into a min-priority queue `std::priority_queue<pair<long long, int>, vector<pair<long long, int>>, greater<>>`.

### Step 3: Relaxation Loop
While the priority queue is not empty:
1. Pop $(d, u)$. If $d > dist[u]$, discard (stale entry).
2. For each neighbor $(v, w)$ of $u$:
   If $dist[u] + w < dist[v]$:
   $$dist[v] = dist[u] + w$$
   Push $(dist[v], v)$ into the priority queue.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((V + E) \log V)$
  Every vertex is extracted from the priority queue at most once. For every edge, we perform at most one priority queue push operation taking $\mathcal{O}(\log V)$.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(V + E)$
  Required for storing the adjacency list and the distance array.
